title: Guilt without sex
summary: Guilt Without Sex is a light-hearted humor book, published in Los Angeles in 1985, that examines the everyday guilt that many people carry. It opens by asking what guilt is, observing that a large share of Americans feel guilty all the time, and then turns to a long run of short, comic scenarios illustrating the condition. Each example is a small, relatable moment: straightening the apartment before the cleaning lady arrives, rooting for the bull at a bullfight, pretending a limp after parking in a handicapped space, barking at the building manager in a no-pets building, or taking the last wooden hanger in the closet. The examples are brief, mostly one or two sentences, and rely on self-deprecating recognition rather than argument or advice. The excerpt presented here consists of these examples and the introduction, so it does not develop a systematic theory of guilt or offer therapeutic remedies, though the book's premise suggests that such guilt is a familiar and amusing part of ordinary life.
